SHORT_TITLE_EXPANDED.weight: medium-to-bold display weight; never light, thin, or hairline
SHORT_TITLE_EXPANDED.tracking: neutral to slightly expanded only when it increases the title silhouette
SHORT_TITLE_EXPANDED.rule: A short title must become a deliberate visual object through scale, weight, stacking, or controlled edge interaction; it must not read as a small label floating in unused space.

STANDARD_TITLE_BLOCK.weight: regular-to-semibold editorial display weight with robust strokes
STANDARD_TITLE_BLOCK.tracking: natural tracking with balanced line lengths
STANDARD_TITLE_BLOCK.rule: Reflow for one compact title silhouette before reducing size.

LONG_TITLE_STACK.weight: regular-to-medium editorial display weight with robust strokes
LONG_TITLE_STACK.tracking: natural tracking and semantic line breaks
LONG_TITLE_STACK.rule: Use balanced semantic line breaks; never compress the complete title into a small dense paragraph.

MICRO_SUBTITLE.rule: Keep the phrase quiet but fully legible at full size and attach it to the title axis, baseline, mask edge, frame, or one named support zone.

SUPPORTING_DECK.rule: Treat an exact longer subtitle as a readable deck, not micro-text; keep it to one or two deliberate lines attached to the title cluster.

category_label.rule: Keep the category subordinate but readable and place it on the same alignment system as the title cluster.

global.title_contrast_target: at least 3:1 against every region crossing the visible glyphs
global.support_contrast_target: at least 4.5:1 where feasible; never trade legibility for atmospheric subtlety
global.cluster_rule: FINAL_TITLE, CATEGORY_LABEL, and MICRO_SUBTITLE or SUPPORTING_DECK must read as one typographic cluster using a shared edge, axis, baseline, frame, mask, or tangent; do not scatter the three roles into unrelated corners.
global.thumbnail_rule: At 25% size the exact title is immediately readable and is the first reading event; support copy may become quiet but must remain structurally attached.
